term: actual cause/effect, nonoverlap, necessary parts and restricted cosmos in #10
definition: C is the aggregate of all wholly contingent things, where wholly contingent means having no necessary parts. Causal roles are restricted to actually existing things; a cause cannot overlap its effect, a stronger requirement than mere inequality. The conditional cosmos argument starts from a nonempty ordinary contingent population. Necessary parts and contingent-part extraction are substantive modal/mereological commitments, not definitions of causation or contingency.
